title: Whole-system reduction square for normalized compact-support paths
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l, with R=O_E and its uniformizer ideal I. Use the actual completed integral coefficient sheaves, strict system calculus, and the normalized constant scalar restrictions H and U [def-sf-constant-completed-reduction-transport, def-sf-integral-system-operations]. Fix the finite-field datum D with l != char(k), operations o and normalized Realizations r. Let e,t be finite unary geometric expressions with common output T, separated at all intermediate schemes and satisfying the full recorded strict origin/amplitude domain and IntegralDomain at K [def-pur-compact-support-limit-equation-data]. Write q_e,q_t for reductionComparison and let (s,a) be a prescribed Path from e to t, where s is the whole-system map and a is the completed integral map. Then constantReduction(H(a)) followed by q_t equals q_e followed by U(s), in the derived category of entire strict constant towers. The assertion involves no total-limit map, corner invertibility or cancellation conclusion.

proof.text:
For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, first consider $\gamma_u:j_{2!}\to Ru_*j_{1!}$, before inversion or the outer proper image. Its normalized adjunct is open base change followed by the projection onto the clopen section $(j_1,1_X)$: identity there and zero on its complementary open. The strict proper/open calculus gives this exact map on constant towers. Apply the ringed-refinement coefficient-square theorem on the small diagram sites to the ring-system map $\Delta\underline R\to((P_n)_T)_n$ and input $\Delta H$. Its open scalar maps are $q_j$ and its proper scalar map is the counit-tensor projection; the constant-diagram direct-image comparison is the specified $\chi$. Restrict the resulting coefficient-system square to constant-$R$ towers using the canonical diagram direct-image comparison. This gives, before evaluation,
$$\widetilde\gamma_u\,q_{j_2}=q_{Ru_*j_{1!}}\mathcal R(\gamma_u).$$
The constant/completed comparisons in Step 1 preserve the proper adjunction and the open adjunction, and preserve the clopen projection (its two components remain identity and zero). Therefore their transported $\gamma_u$ is precisely the specified completed refinement constituent. No cartesian hypothesis on the refinement square is used.

proof.text:
Extend the generator squares to contexts. Right whiskering is substitution of the intermediate input, since each generator identity is natural in that input. For left whiskering, suppose $a_Vt=L(\widetilde t)a_W$ and append a letter $F_e$ with strict counterpart $G_e$. For proper image and open extension use the natural comparison $\lambda_e:F_eL(M)\simeq LG_e(M)$ of the direct-image and exact-product limit theorems. For completed pullback use the corresponding comparison on whole normalized quotient systems: reduction and total limit are an adjoint equivalence there, and the pullback substitution theorem gives $\widehat u^*\mathcal L N\simeq\mathcal L F_uN$, naturally for system morphisms. The maps in Steps 3--6 come from such whole-system maps: inverse images, direct images, units, counits, quotient scalar maps and clopen projections are simultaneous diagram-site constructions. Their constant-$R$ restriction is exactly the strict path in the question; no lift from evaluated maps is being selected. Reduction-word comparisons identify each intermediate with the reduction of its complete intermediate object, so these are normalized systems, with the assumed witnesses and bounds. The counit substitution and the word recursion give $a_{eW}=\lambda_eF_e(a_W)$ and $a_{eV}=\lambda_eF_e(a_V)$ in these coordinates. Naturality now gives
$$a_{eV}F_e(t)=\lambda_eF_e(L(\widetilde t))F_e(a_W)=L(G_e\widetilde t)\lambda_eF_e(a_W)=L(G_e\widetilde t)a_{eW}.$$
Induction on the outer word proves arbitrary whiskering. The pullback comparison has been used on these specified normalized systems, without commuting pullback with arbitrary inverse limits.

proof.text: Induct on Path. Identity is map_id. For inverse use the supplied IsIso proofs, functor preservation of inverses, and multiply the square by the inverse maps. For composition use map_comp and paste the two equations through the intermediate reduction comparison. The generator and whiskering cases are the normalization and context results of the preceding steps. Endpoint and explicit intermediate domains supply their hypotheses. This proves the square in the strict derived category, without taking a limit.

theorem compactSupportPathReductionSquare
    (e t : Expression _ I X T) (ge : e.geometric) (gt : t.geometric)
    (we : IsWord e) (wt : IsWord t) (se : SeparatedWord e) (st : SeparatedWord t)
    (K : (e.domain l E o).FullSubcategory) (ht : t.domain l E o K.obj)
    (ie : IntegralDomain l E e K.obj) (it : IntegralDomain l E t K.obj)
    (s : e.systemObj l E o ((inputReduction l E X).obj K.obj) ⟶
      t.systemObj l E o ((inputReduction l E X).obj K.obj))
    (a : (e.evaluate (integralInterpretation l E)).obj K.obj ⟶
      (t.evaluate (integralInterpretation l E)).obj K.obj)
    (h : Path l E D o r hl K.obj e t s a) :
    (GeneratorReduction.constantReduction l E T.left).map
        ((GeneratorReduction.H l E T.left).map a) ≫
        (reductionComparison l E D o r t gt ⟨K.obj, ht⟩).hom =
      (reductionComparison l E D o r e ge K).hom ≫ towerMap l E D o K.obj s
